skill.name: forge
skill.description: Create one new governed harness artifact from a demonstrated need, exact ownership, contract shape, adversarial evaluation, and human review. Use for a genuinely new pack, contract, workflow, rule, or provider-neutral artifact; do not use for bounded edits, routine decision notes, or bulk rewrites.
skill.shortDescription: Create one governed artifact from evidence through review.
skill.defaultPrompt: Use $forge to develop this one harness artifact from an observed need through exact contracts, evaluation, and review.

instructions: Classify the requested outcome as Kernel, Core, Context, Automation, Integration, configuration, or host responsibility before naming an artifact.
Identify the governing contract, canonical owner, possible effects, and why an existing artifact cannot express the need.
Use a decision note only for a rare cross-cutting, security, compatibility, or expensive-to-reverse choice whose rationale cannot live beside the contract.

For every proposed new system namespace, state the birth-decision disposition: mechanically link the exact optional decision when that threshold is met; otherwise explicitly withhold it and explain why the rationale belongs beside the owning contract or artifact.
flexibility: Choose the shortest stable name and smallest coherent artifact boundary that preserve the classified responsibility.
stopConditions: Stop when ownership is ambiguous or the request is actually a bounded edit to an existing artifact.

instructions: Inspect existing manifests, definitions, exclusions, contracts, and migration bindings for overlapping responsibility.
When overlap exists, extend or correct the current owner instead of creating a second authority.
State the exact gap that remains after the territory review.
stopConditions: Stop when an existing owner already satisfies the requested outcome or the intended relationship cannot be made explicit.

instructions: Create an isolated development workspace before drafting and verify that it is not the protected root checkout.
Reproduce an exact missing contract, failing behavior, or representative pressure case without the proposed artifact.
Use a fresh contained evaluator when available and judge from artifacts; if independent containment is unavailable, record the missing evidence rather than manufacturing a baseline.
flexibility: A deterministic contract failure can replace a stochastic worker baseline when it directly proves the missing invariant.
stopConditions: Stop when no real failure or missing contract justifies a new durable artifact.

instructions: Derive the artifact shape from its governing contract and include identity, ownership, purpose, dependencies, effects, limitations, verification, and migration impact.
Counter every observed baseline rationalization with a mechanical invariant or explicit procedural safeguard.
Keep provider details in Integration, domain meaning in Context, orchestration in Automation, runtime authority in Core, and host delivery in adapters.
flexibility: Use prose for judgment and deterministic code or schemas for rules that can be enforced mechanically.
stopConditions: Stop when the draft would introduce hidden authority, an undeclared dependency, or a duplicate canonical source.

instructions: Run the changed-scope static, graph, fixture, privacy, and behavior checks required by the artifact's claims.
Plant at least one realistic pressure or mutation that would pass if the new boundary were merely documented rather than enforced.
Inspect artifacts and traces instead of accepting the implementing agent's completion statement as evidence.
flexibility: Add broader gates only when a changed transitive artifact or generated graph makes their previous evidence stale.
stopConditions: Stop adoption on any unresolved correctness, security, privacy, authority, migration, or claim-boundary failure.

instructions: Present the exact artifact diff, baseline, adversarial evidence, limitations, stale evidence impact, and rollback or retirement boundary.
Apply review corrections and rerun only the evidence invalidated by those corrections.
Keep merge, publication, installation, configuration, and host realization as separate effects requiring their own authority.
stopConditions: Stop before adopting the artifact without the requested human decision and every applicable gate.

verification: The artifact has one exact canonical owner and no overlapping authority.
Every proposed new system namespace states an exact linked-or-withheld birth-decision disposition and rationale.
A real missing contract or behavior establishes why the artifact exists.
Applicable adversarial checks fail without the boundary and pass with it.
Privacy, effects, evidence maturity, migration impact, and limitations remain explicit.
Adoption, publication, installation, and realization remain separate authorized actions.

gotchas.summary: A trivial or leading baseline can produce a favorable verdict without demonstrating that the new guidance changes difficult behavior.
gotchas.countermeasure: Use a substantive multi-step pressure case or a deterministic missing-contract mutation.

gotchas.summary: A compliant evaluator may create the scenario's fake files, decisions, branches, or external effects as real artifacts.
gotchas.countermeasure: Use isolated containment, prohibit external and publication effects, inspect the diff, and remove only known test scaffolding before review.

gotchas.summary: A schema-valid artifact can still have no runtime, no applicable evidence, or a broken ownership boundary.
gotchas.countermeasure: Match every claim to the verification ladder level and exact evidence that can actually prove it.

gotchas.summary: Drafting on the protected root checkout risks mixing experimental changes with the verified baseline.
gotchas.countermeasure: Verify an isolated worktree and branch before the first edit.

limitations: This procedural guide has no file-write, merge, publication, installation, realization, or external-effect authority.
Adoption requires independent exact host-skill behavior evidence and a separate governed fallback-removal decision.
